title: The Poor Miller's Boy and the Cat
summary: An aging miller who had no children announced to his three apprentices that whoever brought him the finest horse should inherit the mill, while the others must seek their fortunes...
keywords: the poor miller's boy and the cat
full_text:
An aging miller who had no children announced to his three apprentices that whoever brought him the finest horse should inherit the mill, while the others must seek their fortunes elsewhere. The two older apprentices were clever and boastful, while the youngest, Hans, was considered simple and mocked by everyone.

The apprentices set out into the world. In the woods, the older two abandoned Hans to wander alone. Hans reached an enchanted clearing where he met a small, elegant tabby cat who asked him where he was going. Hans explained his quest for a horse. "Serve me faithfully for seven years," said the cat, "and I will give you the most magnificent steed on earth."

Hans agreed. He chopped wood with silver axes, carried water in silver pails, and swept the cat's castle, where twelve kittens served as courtiers. Hans never complained, working with gentle loyalty day after day.

When seven years ended, the cat led Hans to the forest edge and told him to go home; the horse would follow in due time. Hans returned to the mill in rags. His former companions laughed, showing off two lame, half-blind nags they had purchased, and refused Hans shelter in the house, forcing him to sleep in the goose-pen.

The next morning, a dazzling carriage drawn by six magnificent silver stallions rolled into the mill yard, carrying an exquisitely beautiful princess. Stepping down, she revealed herself as the enchanted cat Hans had served so loyally. She presented the old miller with a magnificent horse, gave Hans the grandest estate in the kingdom, and wed the faithful youth in radiant splendor.
moral: The humble and faithful servant receives blessings beyond the dreams of boastful schemers.
